Hi Grace,

Thanks for taking the time on Friday. As part of our procurement/security review we need:

- A current subprocessor inventory showing: name, country, function (e.g., logging, KMS, hosting), whether they process PHI, and data retention scope. CSV preferred.
- Evidence of encryption at rest and KMS ownership (diagram or short note is fine).
- Your completed SIG Lite / CAIQ answers (a few items we flagged for follow-up).

We have a deadline to close the security checklist by next Tuesday (2027-04-06). Can you confirm whether Redwood treats any Horizon-derived data as PHI when configured via the Private deployment options, and whether any downstream backups are retained by subprocessors beyond 30 days?

Attached is our SQ intake PDF with the specific fields we flagged.

Appreciate a short plan for what you can deliver and when.

Best,
Elaine

Horizon Health

Hi Elaine — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary/plan below and an initial deliverable attached.

Plan (deliverables and timing):
- Today (within 2 business hours): high-level subprocessor CSV (attached): subprocessor_inventory_v3.csv — includes PHI flag and retention column.
- Monday (2027-04-05): KMS ownership diagram + short note on key rotation and HSM usage (kms_keyflow_diagram.png).
- Tuesday (2027-04-06 COB): SIG Lite / CAIQ answers for the flagged controls and a PDF evidence index (sig-plus-evidence-index.pdf).

To your specific questions:
- PHI: Redwood does not process PHI by default in Hosted mode. For Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) customers who elect to send PHI, we support configurations to restrict data processing to the private deployment; in those cases the customer is the data controller and Redwood acts as processor. The attached CSV marks the current customer-configured PHI flag per subprocessor where relevant.
- Backups: Our default hosting provider retains snapshots for up to 14 days for recovery; customer-configured Private deployments can opt-out of provider-managed backups. Third-party subprocessors that perform long-term archival are indicated in the CSV and include retention windows. We will call out any subprocessors with >30 day retention.

I attached the CSV with the current roster. Happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk through the highest-risk entries.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Security Programs
Redwood Inference

Attachment: subprocessor_inventory_v3.csv (CSV stub)

Subject: RE: Subprocessor inventory + CAIQ/SIG attachments request

Elaine / Grace — adding a quick technical clarification on KMS and key ownership that often helps auditors:

- For Hosted customers: we manage envelope keys in our KMS; customer data keys are rotated on a 90-day cadence by default. We can provide a KKD (key key derivation) statement and a redacted key rotation ledger for audit.
- For Dedicated/Private installs: customers may bring their own KMS (BYOK) or use a customer-managed Cloud KMS in the customer's account. In BYOK configurations, Redwood never has access to the plaintext customer master key.
- Snapshots / backups: for hosted snapshots that are encrypted with our managed keys, the cloud provider retains encrypted snapshots for up to 14 days. For Private deployments using customer-managed keys, snapshot retention is controlled by the customer.

I'll attach a simple KMS flow diagram and a couple of short notes for your auditors. If KPMG (or your auditor) needs a deeper artifact we can run through a short technical session.

Jonas
Director, Platform Security
Redwood Inference

Attachment: kms_keyflow_diagram.png (PNG stub)

Hi all — KPMG is performing a light SIG review for Horizon as part of the procurement controls. Quick clarifying questions so we can close our findings: 

1) For any subprocessor that performs logging or analytics, do log exports ever leave the provider account unencrypted, or are they always written encrypted and accessible only via IAM with MFA enforced?
2) Which subprocessors (if any) have access to plaintext customer payloads in Hosted mode? Please list names and short purpose.
3) If a subprocessor archives data >30 days, please provide the technical owner and the archive location (region).

We have a DocuSign link to collect signed attestations for any control exceptions — if you could return the CSV with the indicated columns and sign the attestation via the DocuSign link, that would speed up completion: https://docusign.example.com/embedded/abc123

Thanks,

Hi Priya / Elaine — thanks for the questions. Answers below and next steps: 

1) Log exports: All log exports are written encrypted at rest by default. Access is governed by IAM roles; access to logging buckets requires MFA-protected role assumption for provider-managed accounts. We'll include a sample bucket policy in the SIG evidence packet.

2) Access to plaintext payloads in Hosted mode: We do not share plaintext customer payloads with third-party subprocessors as a matter of practice. The only exceptions are post-processing analytics partners for customers who explicitly opt in; those are marked in the attached CSV. Current inventory shows zero Horizon customers flagged for analytics sharing.

3) >30 day archives: The CSV highlights two analytics vendors with optional archival windows; both vendors' archives are in us-central1 and have named technical owners (column: tech_owner). We'll provide the named contacts in the evidence PDF.

Next steps / asks:
- We'll upload the SIG evidence index PDF and the completed CAIQ answers to the HubSpot secure file share and link here by EOD Tuesday (2027-04-06).
- Please sign the attestation via DocuSign.
- If KPMG needs a redacted key rotation ledger or a short technical call, Jonas can host a 30-minute session Wed morning.

Deliverables attached or incoming: subprocessor_inventory_v3.csv, kms_keyflow_diagram.png, sig-plus-evidence-index.pdf (incoming).

Thanks — Grace
